facts.text: Cows have almost 360-degree vision, but they have a blind spot directly in front of their noses.
Cattle are dichromatic, meaning they have two colour-sensitive cone types, so reds and greens are hard for them to tell apart.
Bulls don't charge because of the colour red. It's the movement of the cape that sets them off.
A cow has one stomach with four compartments: the rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum.
Cows spend around eight hours a day chewing their cud.
A cow can produce well over 100 litres of saliva a day.
Cows are ruminants, which means they ferment plant material in a specialised stomach before digesting it.
Cows can chew well over 40 times a minute while eating.
A dairy cow typically drinks around 100 litres of water a day, and more in hot weather.
Cows can doze standing up, but they lie down for the deeper stages of sleep.
Cows spend roughly 10 to 12 hours a day lying down, resting and ruminating.
Cows have a keen sense of smell, well beyond what humans can detect.
Every cow has a unique muzzle pattern, a bit like a human fingerprint.
Cows can recognise familiar herd mates by their faces.
Cows form strong social bonds, and separating them from their companions causes measurable stress.
Herds have social hierarchies, and cows groom each other to maintain their relationships.
Cows can hear sounds both higher and lower in pitch than humans can.
Cows have individually recognisable moos, and a mother responds to her own calf's call.
A healthy calf can usually stand and walk within an hour or so of being born.
A calf can pick out its mother's moo from the noise of the whole herd.
A cow's pregnancy lasts around nine months, close to a human's.
Cows almost always have a single calf, and twins are rare.
A cow's udder has four quarters, each with its own teat and its own milk supply.
There are more than 1,000 recognised breeds of cattle worldwide.
Holstein cattle are usually black and white, and Jersey cattle are typically light brown.
Cattle are farmed on every continent except Antarctica.
Cows don't have upper front teeth. They press grass against a tough pad instead.
Cows chew with a side-to-side grinding motion rather than up and down.
A dairy cow typically produces around 25 to 30 litres of milk a day.
Cows can spend up to two-thirds of the day eating and chewing.
Cows have wide-set eyes that give them a broad field of view, and they're quick to notice movement.
Cattle are social animals and can become distressed when kept on their own.
What do you call a cow with no legs? Ground beef.
What do you call a cow with two legs? Lean beef.
What do you call a lazy cow? A couch potato.
Why do cows wear bells? Because their horns don't work.
What do you call a cow that just had a calf? De-calf-inated.
What do you call a cow that plays the guitar? A moo-sician.
Why did the cow go to the cinema? To see the moo-vie.
Why did the cow cross the road? To get to the udder side.
